feature1.name: feature_intro
feature1.label: Name Styles
feature1.title: Band Name Generator: Styles by Genre
feature1.description: Every genre has its own naming logic. Pick one in the band name generator above, or scan the styles below to see how the conventions differ.

items.title: Rock
items.description: Rock names pair a worn image with a strong noun: think 'Wild Static' or 'The Crimson Roses'. They should sound right spray-painted on an amp and shouted from a crowd.

items.title: Metal
items.description: Metal reaches for weight and myth: 'Ashen Covenant' or 'Sunless Vigil' promise volume, ritual, and doom. Concrete, physical words beat clever puns here.

items.title: Indie / alternative
items.description: Indie names are handmade and a little wry: 'Paper Coastline' or 'The Borrowed Sweaters' feel like they were coined in a practice space, not a boardroom.

items.title: Emo / post-hardcore
items.description: Emo names confess: 'October Motel' or 'Sleepless Theory' carry homesickness and hurt in three syllables. Nostalgic, specific, and easy to tattoo.

items.title: Pop
items.description: Pop names are bright and instantly chantable: 'Cherry Cinema' or 'Fizzy Galaxy' read as hooks before anyone hears a note. If a room can sing it back, it works.

items.title: Electronic / dance
items.description: Electronic names borrow from machines and texture: 'Glacial Voltage' or 'Parallel Echo' sound like they were built in a DAW — synthetic, precise, and atmospheric.

items.title: Hip-hop / rap
items.description: Hip-hop names carry swagger and place: 'Uptown Cipher' or 'Concrete Dynasty' tell you who they are and which block they're from in two words.

how_to_use.name: how_to_use
how_to_use.label: HOW TO USE
how_to_use.title: How to Choose a Band Name
how_to_use.description: Run these three tests on every idea your band name generator produces — they separate a name you'll keep from a name you'll outgrow.

items.title: Say it out loud
items.description: Announce it like a frontman, answer it in an interview, text it to a friend. If it's hard to say or spell after one hearing, it will fight you for the life of the band.

items.title: Search it before you love it
items.description: Search the exact name in quotes, then on streaming services and social platforms. A name nobody else uses is easier to own than one you'll always be disambiguating.

items.title: Fit the room you'll play
items.description: Picture the name on the marquee of the venue you actually want to play. Genre-appropriate, memorable, and a little distinctive beats clever-but-generic every time.

feature2.name: feature_benefits
feature2.label: Before You Claim It
feature2.title: The Band Name Availability Checklist
feature2.description: This band name generator never claims a name is free. Instead it hands you the exact checks to run yourself — every result card links straight to them.

items.title: Exact web search
items.description: Search the name in quotes plus 'band'. If the first page belongs to someone else's project, move on — you'd be competing for your own name forever.

items.title: Streaming platforms
items.description: Look the name up on Spotify and Apple Music. Distros reject names that collide with existing artist profiles, so settle this before your first release.

items.title: Social handles
items.description: Check the handle on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. You don't need every platform, but the ones your audience lives on should be close to the name itself.

items.title: Domain name
items.description: A matching .com is ideal but not required — 'nameband.com' or 'nameofficial.com' are standard fallbacks. Grab the domain the day you commit.

items.title: Trademark screening
items.description: For anything beyond a hobby, search your national trademark register (USPTO in the US). This is screening, not legal clearance — a trademark attorney makes the final call.

items.title: Sleep on it
items.description: Live with the shortlist for a week. The name that still feels right on a Tuesday morning, after the excitement fades, is the one to claim.

items.title: Can I use a generated band name for my real band?
items.description: Yes — every name this free band name generator produces is an invented suggestion you're free to use, change, or discard, at no cost. The tool does not run trademark or platform checks, so run the availability checklist yourself before you commit the name to releases and profiles.

items.title: What does the no-AI mode actually do?
items.description: No-AI mode lets the band name generator skip the model entirely. It combines fixed, genre-specific word lists through classic band-name templates — 'adjective + noun', 'the + adjective + noun', 'noun & the collective' — and shows you the exact template behind every name. It's instant, transparent, and never labels a word-list result as AI-written.

items.title: Is the availability checklist a legal clearance?
items.description: No. The checklist links to Google, streaming services, social platforms, domain search, and trademark registers so you can look yourself. It is practical screening, not legal advice — for real protection, have a trademark attorney run a proper clearance search before you invest in the name.

items.title: How do I generate one-word band names?
items.description: Set Name length to 'One word'. The band name generator then returns single words — real words, compounds, or invented words that still read naturally. One-word names are the easiest to own but the hardest to find free, so check them extra carefully.

items.title: Can I build the name around my own keywords?
items.description: Yes. Put a keyword, city, era, or influence in the keywords field — 'ravens', 'Detroit garage', '80s synth club' — and the band name generator anchors its directions around it. In no-AI mode your keyword becomes the anchor word of the template.

items.title: Does it work for metal, rock, emo, or hip-hop names specifically?
items.description: Yes. In the band name generator, the Genre control rewrites the naming logic for each style: metal gets weight and myth, emo gets confession and nostalgia, electronic gets machines and texture, hip-hop gets swagger and place. Pick your genre and the conventions follow.

items.title: Is the first generation really free?
items.description: Yes. This band name generator is completely free — every generation works without an account or sign-in. Pick your genre, vibe, and keywords, and generate as often as you like.
